incident.title: Unauthorised vessel within dam wall exclusion zone
incident.involved_parties: Sample Worker A (Horticulturist); Sample Worker B (Grounds and Catchment Officer)
incident.location: Whole of GAWB / Lake Awoonga recreation area
incident.description: During a pontoon mooring inspection at the dam wall, two workers observed a recreational vessel inside the marked exclusion zone. The workers photographed the vessel, alerted the operator, and directed the vessel out of the restricted area. The operator complied immediately.
incident.basic_event: Recreational vessel operated inside the dam wall exclusion zone during a mooring inspection
incident.injuries: Nil injuries or damage. Potential consequence: unauthorised access to critical water infrastructure.
incident.immediate_actions: Workers instructed the vessel to leave the exclusion zone; photographs taken; Queensland Police report submitted; incident notified to Natural Resources and Recreation Manager and Health and Safety Manager.

assumptions: Investigation limited to the security response process; police evidence not available to the investigation team at time of reporting.
basic_cause: Exclusion zone signage and patrol presence did not deter recreational vessel entry before workers identified the breach.

absent_failed.text: Detection: exclusion zone breach relied on incidental observation by nearby workers
absent_failed.reason: No scheduled surveillance of the zone at that hour

absent_failed.text: Warning: no audible or visual alarm on zone entry
absent_failed.reason: Warning system not installed for water-side zone

individual_team.text: Hazard recognition delayed until visual sighting
individual_team.reason: Breach only identified after entering line of sight

task_env.text: Large water area with limited sight lines from patrol vantage points
task_env.reason: Geometry of dam wall limits observation coverage

organisational.text: Risk assessment for recreation access did not schedule surveillance controls for early morning
Public communication of exclusion zone boundaries limited to signage

people.text: Workers identified the breach and responded correctly and promptly
Vessel operator did not recognise the exclusion zone boundary

environment.text: Large water area with limited sight lines from patrol vantage points

equipment.text: No audible or visual alarm on exclusion zone entry

procedures.text: Detection relied on incidental observation by nearby workers; no scheduled surveillance
Recreation access risk assessment did not identify early morning as a higher-risk period

organisation.text: Public communication of exclusion zone boundaries limited to signage
Control verification due date exceeded for the recreation access risk assessment

conclusions: The investigation concluded the breach occurred because scheduled surveillance and warning controls for the exclusion zone were absent during early morning hours, and public awareness of the zone relied on signage alone.

recommendations.text: Extend scheduled surveillance coverage of the dam wall exclusion zone to include early morning periods, using existing camera and patrol resources.
Review and refresh public communication of exclusion zone boundaries across boat ramp signage and recreation publications.

learnings: Exclusion zones around critical infrastructure require surveillance scheduling matched to actual access patterns, not only daylight patrol periods.
Positive finding: workers responded correctly and promptly, using photography and direct engagement without placing themselves at risk.

cap.recommendation: Extend surveillance coverage to early morning periods

timeline.event: Workers arrive at dam wall to inspect pontoon moorings
Workers observe recreational vessel inside exclusion zone
Workers photograph vessel and direct operator from zone
Police report submitted with photo evidence
Incident notified to Recreation Manager and H&S Manager

fivewhys.question: Why was the vessel inside the exclusion zone?
fivewhys.answer: The operator launched at a public ramp and proceeded past signage without recognising the boundary.

fivewhys.question: Why was the breach not detected earlier?
fivewhys.answer: No scheduled surveillance of the zone during early morning; detection relied on nearby workers.

fivewhys.question: Why was surveillance not scheduled?
fivewhys.answer: Recreation access risk assessment did not identify early morning as a higher-risk period.

fivewhys.question: Why did the risk assessment miss this period?
fivewhys.answer: Assessment was last reviewed before patrol schedules changed and was overdue for revalidation.

fivewhys.question: Why was the overdue review not actioned?
fivewhys.answer: No monitoring trigger existed for overdue risk assessment reviews in the recreation area program.

evidence.description: Scene photographs of vessel within exclusion zone
Witness statement - Grounds and Catchment Officer

plan.scope: Investigate the circumstances of the unauthorised vessel entry, the adequacy of exclusion zone controls, and the security response process.
plan.objectives: Establish facts; identify absent or failed defences and organisational factors; recommend corrective actions per the hierarchy of controls.
plan.team: Lead Investigator plus Safety Systems Specialist
plan.method: ICAM per MPR-INT-0214; PEEPO data collection; witness interviews per Appendix D

witness.name: Sample Worker B
witness.location: Lake Awoonga dam wall pontoon area
witness.statement: We were checking pontoon moorings when we noticed a boat inside the exclusion zone near the dam wall. I observed Sample Worker A photograph the vessel and get the operator's attention. The operator was told to leave the area immediately and complied. The vessel registration was recorded and passed to police.

approval.name: Sample Manager E
approval.conditions: Approved with one condition: the recommended surveillance coverage change is to be verified against the current recreation risk assessment before implementation sign-off.
